reasoning.text: The render reads well already — the ISO and TOP views clearly show the eight glass BRAM banks down the -X edge, the conflict-free crossbar spine, the copper multiplier column with its dark/steel symmetric add-sub pairs, the Barrett reduction spine, the twiddle ROM, the control cluster, and the exploded radix-4 legend lifted on +Z risers. The X-ray test passes (no subsystem is swallowed) and the elevation views show no stray floaters. The one clear constitution violation is the heatsink: ten separate `heatsink_fin_0..9` parts plus a baseplate model pure decoration as eleven parts — exactly the 'collapse 10 heatsink_fin_* → one finned heatsink' anti-pattern. The fin array carries no subsystem information and inflates the part count without raising information density.
gaps: Source-fidelity ceiling (cannot be closed in the visual pass): bank()/offset(), the per-stage crossbar permutation sigma_s, the twiddle-ROM rearranged-loop address f(stage,block), and the FSM transition table are committed [conv] placeholders, not the paper's Sec.III scheme — these must come from the verify/evidence leg, not the geometry.

Open question for next iteration: whether the 8 lanes' mult/add/sub/reg (32 parts) should collapse to 8 single `bu` parts per the over-decomposition rule. Kept this pass because the copper-multiplier / dark-adder / steel-subtractor color coding is the ONLY array-scale depiction of the symmetric-operator sharing (the exploded legend shows radix-4 internals, not the radix-2 lane); collapsing would lower internal legibility. Re-evaluate the trade.

The consolidated heatsink lost its finned silhouette (now a plain box); acceptable since the cooler is incidental hardware, not a machine subsystem, but a single low-fin-relief shape could recover a little recognizability cheaply.

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.bank_index: b(i) = (i&7) ^ ((i>>3)&7) ^ ((i>>6)&7) ^ ((i>>9)&1)   (committed GF(2)-linear XOR-fold; distinct banks for every power-of-two stride incl. 512)
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); because the bank function is GF(2)-linear, b(i) XOR b(i+2^s) = fold(2^s) != 0, so the two operands always land in distinct banks; the crossbar applies the induced read permutation sigma_s mapping lane l <- bank(base_s + l*stride_s) and the write-back applies sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which the XOR-fold guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle
params.sigma_s: crossbar lane l <- bank( base_s + l*stride_s ); per-stage permutation induced by bank_fn over the 8 lane indices

before.notes:
Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.
[conv] COMMITTED conflict-free map: bank(i)=XOR-fold of the four index groups of i (low three 3-bit groups plus bit 9 — for N=1024 only bit 9 lies above the offset field), offset(i)=floor(i/8). This is a GF(2)-linear bank function, so for any power-of-two stride 2^k the two operands differ in exactly one address bit and bank(i) XOR bank(i+2^k) = fold(2^k) != 0 -> operands always in distinct banks. [calc] FIXES the verifier counterexample of the prior map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: there b(i+512)=b(i) (576 mod 8 = 0) so stride-512 operands collided; with XOR-fold fold(bit9)->bank bit0 = 1 != 0. (bank,offset) is a bijection on [0,1024) (offset fixes bits 9..3, low 3 bits XOR-map to all 8 banks). All human-facing annotations (crossbar/addr_gen/bram) now cite this single committed map with the (i>>9)&1 high term; the prior additive form b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 has been removed as a buggy duplicate. [source-missing] the paper's exact sigma_s crossbar permutation table per stage is not transcribed; the XOR-fold realizes the named property (per-stage 8-way distinctness) but may differ in routing from the paper's specific construction.
sigma_s = the routing induced by addr_gen_unit's bank() at stage stride 2^s [conv]. The paper's explicit per-stage crossbar permutation table is [source-missing]; committed here as the bank-map-induced permutation so the topology is single-valued (impl2 left sigma_s undefined, impl1 used a different fold).

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

before.notes:
Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1.

transitions: IDLE -> LOAD  [host start pulse]

STAGE_LOOP -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [enter next twiddle-sharing block]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
BUTTERFLY -> REDUCE  [lane products valid]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
STAGE_LOOP -> DRAIN  [forward-only transform done]
INTT_STAGE_LOOP -> SCALE_N_INV  [inverse stages done]
SCALE_N_INV -> DRAIN  [coefficients scaled by N^-1]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

fields.before: EXPLODED ABOVE: aluminum heatsink baseplate that clamps onto the FPGA package lid covering the whole die, lifted high (y=3.6) on a long riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine — keeping the die floorplan and the +X pipeline-register column visible in the ISO X-ray rather than swallowing them; carries ten fins at 0.3 pitch.
fields.after: EXPLODED ABOVE: the aluminum finned heatsink that clamps onto the FPGA package lid over the whole die, lifted high on a riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine — keeping the die floorplan and the +X pipeline-register column visible in the ISO X-ray rather than swallowing them. Ten 0.12 m fins at 0.3 m pitch over a 3x4 m baseplate, modeled as ONE finned block (the fin comb is decoration captured in spec, not ten separate parts).

after.notes: Consolidated finned heatsink — the prior ten heatsink_fin_* parts were pure decoration and have been collapsed into this single block with the fin geometry recorded in params (anti-decoration rule).

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic, then scribe three thin floorplan partition lines dividing the die into memory, butterfly-array and reduction/control zones; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view; add two +X dataflow arrows (mult->add/sub, add/sub->register) on the exploded unit and a thin carbon-fiber fusion-callout strut from the lanes-6/7 yoke up to the exploded baseplate so the W1->W2->W3->j-rotator->add/sub->register order and the represented fused unit are unambiguous, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink high onto its riser stub well above the die so the datapath below stays visible.
